title: 'His Father Will Handle Everything': Family of Kochi Crash Victim Fears Case Is Being Weakened
excerpt: Three 21-year-old students — Iyas, Devika and Gopika — were killed when a Mini Cooper rammed their scooter near Nedumbassery on October 11. Gopika's father alleges the accused's family is using its influence, and questions why the 19-year-old driver was sent to a borstal school.
body:
• Three students, all 21 — Iyas, Devika and Gopika — died on October 11 when a speeding Mini Cooper rammed their scooter from behind near Nedumbassery, Kochi.
  • The accused driver, Suhail Sajeev, 19, was detained at the scene and the car impounded; police are examining whether he was under the influence of alcohol.
  • Gopika's father, M.R. Pradeep Kumar, alleged on Tuesday that the accused's family is using its influence to interfere with the investigation, and questioned the decision to send Suhail to the Borstal School at Thrikkakara instead of a regular prison.
  • An eyewitness told ANI the driver said after the crash that his father would "handle everything" — a remark that has fuelled public anger and a viral video of the car being gifted to him by his mother.

The family of one of three students killed in a crash near Kochi's Nedumbassery on October 11 has said publicly what many in Kerala have been saying since the accident: they fear the case against the young man at the wheel will be quietly weakened. M.P. Gopika, 21, died with two friends, Iyas and Devika, when a luxury Mini Cooper rammed the scooter the three were riding. The accused driver, Suhail Sajeev, 19, was detained by police at the scene and the vehicle impounded.

The allegation

Speaking in Palakkad on Tuesday, Gopika's father M.R. Pradeep Kumar alleged that the accused's family was using its influence to interfere with the investigation, and said he feared his daughter would not get justice, The Hindu reported. "Soon after the incident, the accused said his father would take care of everything. We believe this shows the influence he has," Mr. Kumar said. An eyewitness account carried by ANI records the same remark from the scene: confronted by local residents after the collision, the driver said his father would "handle everything," while the three injured students lay unmoving on the road.

Mr. Kumar also questioned the decision to send Suhail to the Borstal School at Thrikkakara — a detention facility for offenders aged 18 to 21 — instead of a regular prison. Separately, a video showing the accused's mother gifting him the car on his birthday, calling it his "dream car," has resurfaced and spread widely since the crash, hardening public sentiment. Police are examining whether the accused was driving under the influence of alcohol, and a case has been registered.

Why this case is resonating

Kerala records thousands of road deaths a year, and fatal crashes involving young drivers of high-powered cars gifted by affluent parents have become a recurring public argument in the state — about licensing, enforcement, and whether influence bends outcomes. The families' demand is procedural, not rhetorical: a transparent investigation, timely forensic and medical examination, and charges that match the evidence. What happens in the next steps — the framing of charges and any move to add further accused, as some reports suggest the families are seeking — will determine whether those fears are answered or confirmed.
